chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ali ibn Shajara, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged regarding the waterway of the valley of Mahzour: for the palm trees, the water can reach up to the two ankles, and for the farmers (of grain), up to the two shoe-straps.
ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic legal limits for water irrigation for palm trees and grain crops according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This ruling from Wadi Mahzour illustrates the Prophet’s practical application of *israf* (wastefulness) in agricultural management, a principle highly valued in Shia jurisprudence for sustaining community resources. By setting distinct depth limits for date palms versus grain, the hadith emphasizes proportional water usage based on crop needs, reinforcing the ethical obligation to conserve water as a divine trust (*amanah*).

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Ali Bin Shajara, from Hafs Bin Giyas, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> judged regarding a waterway of the valley of Mahzour, for the palm trees it can be up to the two ankles, and for the farmers up to the two shoe-straps’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Ali ibn Shajarah Hafs ibn Ghiyath who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, issued a judgment about the flood water of valley of Mahzur for palm trees up to the anklebones and for plantation up to shoelaces.”
